descripcion: At B2 the goal is to fix the most common verb-noun collocations of everyday and simple professional English: make a decision, take a risk, have an effect. These are not interchangeable with do or take at random — each noun has its own fixed partner.

ejemplos.texto: We need to make a decision by tomorrow.
It's worth taking the risk, in my opinion.
The change had a big effect on the whole team.

notas: These verbs aren't interchangeable: to do a decision or to make a risk both sound wrong to a native speaker.
Have is the default verb for many abstract nouns: have an effect, have an impact, have a problem.
Make an effort is one of the most common collocations in everyday spoken English.

es.en: Spanish tomar covers several of these collocations (tomar una decisión – make a decision, tomar un riesgo – take a risk), which English splits between make and take. That single difference explains most confusion between the two verbs.
es.es: El español «tomar» cubre varias de estas colocaciones («tomar una decisión» – «make a decision», «tomar un riesgo» – «take a risk»), que el inglés reparte entre «make» y «take». Esa única diferencia explica la mayor parte de la confusión entre ambos verbos.

de.en: German machen leads to make a photo (ein Foto machen) where English says take a photo, and eine Entscheidung treffen gives no clue that English uses make. The make/take split has to be learned pair by pair.
de.de: Deutsches «machen» führt zu «make a photo» aus «ein Foto machen», wo Englisch «take a photo» sagt, und «eine Entscheidung treffen» gibt keinen Hinweis darauf, dass Englisch «make» verwendet. Die Unterscheidung «make/take» muss paarweise gelernt werden.

it.en: Italian fare leads to make a photo (fare una foto) where English says take, and prendere un caffè to take a coffee where English says have. The make/take/have split has to be learned pair by pair.
it.it: «Fare» porta a «make a photo» da «fare una foto», mentre l'inglese dice «take»; «prendere un caffè» porta a «take a coffee», mentre l'inglese dice «have». La divisione «make/take/have» va imparata collocazione per collocazione.

fr.en: French faire leads to make a photo (faire une photo) where English says take, and prendre un café to take a coffee where English says have. The make/take/have split has to be learned pair by pair.
fr.fr: «Faire» conduit à «make a photo» à partir de «faire une photo», alors que l'anglais dit «take», et «prendre un café» à «take a coffee», alors que l'anglais dit «have». Le trio «make/take/have» doit s'apprendre collocation par collocation.

pt.en: Portuguese tirar uma foto corresponds well to take a photo, but tomar um café leads to take a coffee where English says have. The make/take/have split has to be learned pair by pair.
pt.pt: «Tirar uma foto» corresponde bem a «take a photo», mas «tomar um café» pode levar a «take a coffee», enquanto o inglês usa «have». A divisão «make/take/have» precisa ser aprendida par a par.

errores: Using do as a default verb for every collocation.
Saying make a risk instead of take a risk.
Saying do an effort instead of make an effort.

redemittel.expresion: Is it make or do here?

traducciones.de: Heisst es hier machen oder tun?
traducciones.it: Qui si dice fare o compiere?

autochequeo: Have I chosen the right verb for each noun, not defaulted to do?
Have I used make and take correctly, not interchangeably?
Does the combination sound natural to a native speaker?
Have I used at least four different collocations?
Have I avoided do as a catch-all verb?
